summary: Over 14 days, CGM coverage is good and overall time in range is high, but time below range is elevated, with the strongest lows overnight around 01:00 local and a second cluster after the afternoon peak around 19:00. Carbs were not logged, so UAM/SMB and Dynamic ISF carried meal dosing while profile CR stayed unused. The only supported first profile review is raising the 00:00 target to add overnight buffer; basal, CR, ISF, DIA, and AAPS levers should stay unchanged in the same step.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM quality is good: 3995 valid entries, 98.7 percent coverage, about 5-minute cadence, 10 gaps, largest gap 65 minutes, no invalid or duplicate points. First and last days are partial. Local timezone is BST. The selected aaps_profile is complete and profile_context marks historical applicability as yes. Included telemetry is thinner for treatments, loop snapshots, and events, and there are zero carb or e-carb entries.
analysis_steps.evidence: telemetry.data_quality status good; treatment_summary carb_entries 0 and total_carbs_g 0; included_counts show sampled treatments and loop statuses; hourly_glucose_local has 24 rows; profile_context.historical_applicability yes.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No activity, alcohol, or meal-composition log. Only sampled treatments and loop statuses. Dilution implied by the u200 profile name is not quantified.

analysis_steps.findings: Mean glucose 121.6 mg/dL, time in range 86.0 percent, time above range 8.9 percent, time below range 5.1 percent, CV 32.6 percent. Severe lows reach 41-42 mg/dL and highs reach 290-293 mg/dL. Local hypo burden is highest at 01:00 (TBR 18.5 percent) and 19:00 (TBR 15.3 percent), with additional overnight TBR near 10-11 percent. 04:00-08:00 is the safest fasting-like window. GLP-1 1.25 mg notes, an 08-19 occlusion, and site or sensor changes are safety confounders. Wide max IOB and max basal do not constrain stacked insulin.
analysis_steps.evidence: glucose_summary; hourly_glucose_local TBR and means; glucose_extremes; representative_events for GLP-1, site change, sensor change, occlusion; sample loop IOB up to about 4.7-5.9 U.
analysis_steps.dependencies: data_quality coverage is adequate for safety pattern calls; meal and activity labels are not.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Cannot split hypo cause among residual IOB, target, basal, GLP-1, exercise, set failure, or sensor artifact without fasting and activity labels.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight target 90 mg/dL sits on the overnight mean while 00:00-03:00 TBR is high, and some night loop rows still raise temp basal near 90 mg/dL. Daytime target 100 mg/dL is below afternoon means, but meals and UAM remain plausible. 00:00 basal 0.6 U/h lines up with the overnight hypo window but is not isolated from leftover IOB. 05:00-08:00 looks stable. 16:00 basal 0.5 U/h sits under the afternoon peak, and 19:00 basal rises into the evening crash; both are meal- and IOB-confounded.
analysis_steps.evidence: target_segments 90/100/90; basal_segments 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.7, 0.5, 0.6, 0.7 U/h; hourly_glucose_local 00:00-03:00, 14:00-19:00, and 04:00-08:00; representative loop statuses with night up-dosing and high afternoon temps.
analysis_steps.dependencies: safety_overview hypo clusters forbid adding overnight or late-evening insulin. data_quality has no labeled fasting stretches.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No true fasting experiment. Mid-period profile-switch notes and GLP-1 start on 08-14 can change overnight need. Delivered temps often differ from the profile curve.

analysis_steps.findings: CR segments exist but were unused because carb entries and COB are zero. Profile ISF is flat 56 mg/dL/U, while Dynamic ISF is on and sample variable_sens spans about 28-124 mg/dL/U, so 56 is not the operational ISF. Correction windows are contaminated by later rises or large stacked drops and cannot validate ISF. DIA 10 h is long and can keep afternoon UAM IOB active at 19:00-03:00, but peak and dilution are unvalidated.
analysis_steps.evidence: carb_ratio_segments; isf_segments 56; dia_hours 10; treatment_summary carb_entries 0; therapy_response_windows mixed rises and overshoots; loop variable_sens and COB 0.
analysis_steps.dependencies: basal_targets overnight IOB versus basal. safety_overview against strengthening ISF while TBR is high.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carb logs, no isolated correction-only nights, no insulin brand or peak beyond free_peak_oref.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are on, SMB is always enabled, and high temp-target SMB is off, which matches zero-carb use and is protective during observed 135 mg/dL temp targets. Delivery is frequent: 3-minute interval, UAM cap 20 minutes. Sample reasons show boost-sized SMBs larger than profile-basal scaling. UAM is the meal engine, not duplicate COB. Overnight lows are better explained by leftover IOB plus target 90 plus some night up-dosing than by UAM left on by mistake.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_enabled, uam_enabled, smb_always_enabled, smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false; smb_interval 3; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes 20; loop reasons COB 0, UAM High Boost, SMB equals 0.4 to 1.6; temp targets 135.
analysis_steps.dependencies: safety_overview evening and overnight TBR. basal_targets and unused CR from earlier stages.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Full SMB stream not included. Boost frequency unknown. No activity log for 18:00-19:00 crashes.

analysis_steps.findings: Autosens is off; Dynamic ISF is on at 70 percent and is the operational sensitivity. max IOB 25 U and max basal 12 U/h are far above about 19.7 U/day total insulin and about 16.2 U/day profile basal, so they do not brake the observed rise-crash. Enacted temps bind nearer 4 U/h via safety multipliers. Carb-absorption settings have no test because COB is unused. Sensitivity_ratio of 1 is a neutral snapshot, not enabled Autosens. Profile ISF and DynISF factor would explain the same pattern, so they must not change together.
analysis_steps.evidence: autosens_enabled false; dynamic_sensitivity_enabled true; dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent 70; max_iob_units 25; max_basal_u_per_hour 12; treatment_summary total_insulin_u 275.95; loop sensitivity_ratio and variable_sens.
analysis_steps.dependencies: automation_smb_uam delivery and boost. profile ISF/DIA hypotheses. safety_overview against more high-BG aggressiveness.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No DynISF TDD source. GLP-1 and the 08-19 occlusion can change apparent sensitivity.

analysis_steps.findings: Declared meal_strategies is an empty list and strategy_stable_for_period is null, so there is no declared prebolus or immediate bolus percent. Observed execution is unannounced meals plus correction-sized doses and UAM. Several midday windows rise for 2 hours after tiny insulin, and several afternoon windows crash by 2-4 hours. No immediate-bolus percentage exists in the package and none is inferred. Adding a large immediate meal bolus on top of current UAM would stack on evening hypo risk.

analysis_steps.dependencies: CR unused. SMB/UAM always on. DIA 10 h and DynISF stack. Daytime target 100 and occasional TT 135.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No declared prebolus_minutes or immediate_bolus_percent. No meal start times or carb grams.

analysis_steps.findings: No e-carb amount, offset, or duration was declared or logged. Extended-carb count is zero. Carb-absorption settings were idle. Afternoon glucose that stays high then falls is compatible with late absorption or with UAM-only catch-up; composition is unknown. E-carbs are not a pump extended bolus and are not a current tactic.
analysis_steps.evidence: treatment_summary extended_carb_entries 0; carb_treatment_entries empty; analysis_context meal_strategies empty; min_5m_carbimpact and meal_max_absorption_hours unused in COB 0 loop reasons.
analysis_steps.dependencies: meal_bolus_strategy unannounced-meal path. automation_smb_uam UAM deviations are not COB.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No meal-linked absorption series. Do not infer e-carb duration from aggregates.

analysis_steps.findings: Ranked explanations: first, unannounced afternoon intake handled late by UAM and DynISF, with DIA 10 h leaving IOB for 19:00 and overnight lows; second, overnight target 90 invites extra loop insulin while overnight means already sit near 90-105 mg/dL; third, 00:00 basal 0.6 U/h may contribute but is not separable from residual IOB; fourth, 16:00 basal 0.5 U/h is not established as the afternoon-high cause. Audit corrections: CR is unused rather than numerically wrong; a sensitivity_ratio of 1 does not mean Autosens is on; remaining temp time is not the SMB interval; UAM is not duplicate COB; package historical_applicability yes overrides any inference that the profile was absent. One conservative family only: raise target 00:00 from 90 to 100 mg/dL. Keep 23:00 target, all basal, CR, ISF, DIA, and all six AAPS groups in this step. Reassess evening crash only after nights are observed.
analysis_steps.evidence: hourly_glucose_local overnight versus afternoon-evening; target 90 versus night loop up-dosing; zero carbs versus UAM/DynISF; decision_inventory complete current values; checkpoints 1-3 plus package override rules.
analysis_steps.dependencies: All prior stages. Do not combine target change with basal, ISF, DynISF, or SMB delivery.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Still no labeled fasting night or logged afternoon meals, so confidence stays medium for the target change and low for meal timing.

strengths: CGM coverage 98.7 percent with regular 5-minute cadence supports clock-time pattern review.
Overall time in range 86.0 percent with average glucose 121.6 mg/dL.
Local 04:00-08:00 is consistently stable, with time in range about 95-99 percent and little hyperglycemia.
High temp-target SMB lockout matches observed 135 mg/dL temp targets and is a useful brake.
The selected profile object is complete, and the user declared it applicable for the period.
issues: Time below range 5.1 percent, with the worst local hour 01:00 at 18.5 percent TBR and means sitting on the 90 mg/dL overnight target.
Recurring afternoon rise (local 14:00-17:00 TAR up to 32 percent) followed by an evening crash (19:00 TBR 15.3 percent, lows to 41 mg/dL).
Glucose variability is high (CV 32.6 percent; SD 39.7 mg/dL), so a 90 mg/dL target leaves little overnight buffer.
Meals were unannounced: zero carb and e-carb entries, COB 0, so CR and the carb-absorption model cannot be tested and UAM/DynISF are compensating.
Automation limits are loose relative to about 20 U/day insulin (max IOB 25 U, preference max basal 12 U/h), allowing stacked high-BG UAM, though they are not the first change family.
Site changes, an occlusion or pump error on 08-19, GLP-1 1.25 mg notes, and a late-period sensor change confound some volatile days.

recommendations.title: Raise the 00:00 overnight target before any insulin-adding change
recommendations.description: Overnight means sit on or under 90 mg/dL while 00:00-03:00 time below range is high, and some night loop rows still increase insulin toward that target. Raising only the 00:00 target adds buffer without increasing basal and without touching SMB or DynISF in the same step.

suggested_change.scope: Applies 00:00-08:00 local. Leave profile.target.23_00 at 90 mg/dL for this single-step review.

recommendations.title: Hold basal, DynISF, and SMB delivery until nights are re-checked
recommendations.description: Afternoon highs and the 19:00 crash have competing explanations in unannounced meals, UAM boosts, DynISF, DIA 10 h, and the 16:00-19:00 basal steps. Changing those now would confound the overnight target test and could worsen lows.

suggested_change.next_family_if_needed: After several nights, review UAM interval or DynISF factor only if the 16:00-19:00 rise-crash remains and overnight TBR has improved.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Change only profile target 00:00 from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL and keep every other profile segment unchanged.
profile_recommendation.rationale: The strongest safety pattern is overnight time below range with local 01:00 TBR 18.5 percent and overnight means near the current 90 mg/dL target. Night loop snapshots still request extra insulin around 90 mg/dL. A 10 mg/dL target rise is a buffer against that up-dosing and does not require deciding whether leftover UAM IOB or 00:00 basal 0.6 U/h is the larger share. Afternoon basal, flat ISF, CR, and DIA remain confounded or unused.
profile_recommendation.next_check: After this single change, compare 3-5 nights of local 00:00-03:00 time below range and 04:00-08:00 averages before considering 23:00 target, 00:00 basal, or any automation change.

parameter_decisions.rationale: This segment overlaps the overnight hypo window, but leftover afternoon UAM IOB and target 90 remain competing causes. Evidence is the 00:00-03:00 TBR cluster plus night temps above 0.6 U/h. Uncertainty is high without a labeled fasting night. Dependency: do not cut basal in the same step as the 00:00 target change.

Local 05:00-06:00 is stable with high time in range and little hyperglycemia. Evidence is hourly_glucose_local TIR 95-97 percent. Uncertainty is residual IOB rather than basal deficit. Dependency: morning stability argues against using this segment to fix overnight lows.

Local 06:00-08:00 remains the strongest fasting-like window. Evidence is TIR 98-99 percent and almost no TAR. Uncertainty is the isolated 08-21 early low near a sensor-change day. Dependency: no increase, because overnight TBR is the binding constraint.

Late-morning rise is more consistent with unannounced intake and late UAM than with a 10:00 basal defect. Evidence is 09:00-12:00 TAR with COB 0 and rising post-correction windows. Uncertainty is meal timing. Dependency: CR and UAM are not separated, so basal stays unchanged.

The lowest basal sits under the highest afternoon glucose, but unannounced carbs and UAM/DynISF chase are equally plausible. Evidence is 14:00-17:00 TAR then 19:00 TBR. Uncertainty is meal composition. Dependency: raising this rate would add insulin into the evening crash and conflicts with the overnight-first order.

18:00 is the start of the crash window, not a proven under-basal. Evidence is local 18:00 TBR 7.7 percent after the 16:00 peak. Uncertainty is stacked IOB versus activity. Dependency: safety_overview forbids adding late-evening insulin.

Basal increases into the worst evening TBR hour. That may add to leftover UAM IOB rather than fix a hole. Evidence is 19:00 TBR 15.3 percent and lows to 41 mg/dL. Uncertainty includes GLP-1 notes and possible activity. Dependency: keep until nights and meal logs separate IOB from basal.
No carb entries use this ratio. Evidence is treatment_summary carb_entries 0 and loop COB 0. Uncertainty is complete for the numeric value. Dependency: meal strategy is UAM, so CR is idle.
Unused during the period. Evidence is zero carb treatments. Uncertainty is high for any CR number. Dependency: do not change CR to compensate for UAM timing.

Daytime rise happened with COB 0, so this CR was not tested. Evidence is late-morning therapy windows that rise after tiny corrections. Uncertainty is meal size. Dependency: hold CR until carbs are logged.

Afternoon peak and crash occurred without announced carbs, so 10.5 g/U is not implicated. Evidence is empty carb_treatment_entries. Uncertainty is high. Dependency: UAM/DynISF, not CR, dosed those hours.

Evening hypos followed unannounced-afternoon dosing, not a logged dinner CR. Evidence is COB 0 and 19:00-23:00 TBR. Uncertainty is leftover IOB. Dependency: keep CR while the first change is overnight target.

Operational ISF is Dynamic ISF, with sample variable_sens far from 56. Therapy windows are not clean ISF tests. Evidence is dynamic_sensitivity_enabled true and mixed correction outcomes. Uncertainty is high for the flat 56 number. Dependency: changing ISF and DynISF would explain the same pattern; change neither with the target.

Overnight means hug 90 mg/dL while 00:00-03:00 TBR is 10-18 percent and night loop rows still raise insulin toward that target. A move to 100 mg/dL matches the existing daytime target and adds buffer without adding basal. Evidence is hourly_glucose_local and night loop statuses. Uncertainty: 04:00-08:00 is already stable, so this also lifts target in a good window; residual IOB may still cause lows. Dependency: do not also change 00:00 basal, 23:00 target, SMB, or DynISF in the same step.

Daytime target is already 100 mg/dL. Afternoon means are higher, but meals and UAM are the likelier drivers. Evidence is 08:00 target segment and 10:00-17:00 TAR with COB 0. Uncertainty is meal timing. Dependency: lowering daytime target would add insulin and conflict with evening TBR.

This segment lasts only until 00:00. 23:00 TBR is present but weaker than 01:00, and one-parameter sequencing prefers changing only 00:00 now. Evidence is 23:00 local TBR 10.1 percent versus 01:00 TBR 18.5 percent. Uncertainty is leftover evening IOB. Dependency: revisit only if 23:00-00:00 lows persist after the 00:00 target change.

Long DIA can keep afternoon UAM active overnight, but peak, dilution, and free_peak_oref are unvalidated. Evidence is 2-4 hour crashes after afternoon dosing plus DIA 10 h. Uncertainty is high. Dependency: DIA, SMB frequency, and DynISF are not separable; keep DIA.

Observed meals were unannounced, so UAM is the meal path. Turning UAM off without a carb or bolus plan would leave the afternoon rise unhandled. Evidence is COB 0 and smb/uam both true. Uncertainty is boost size. Dependency: meal strategy still relies on UAM.

Always-on SMB is consistent with zero COB. High temp-target SMB off is protective and matches 135 mg/dL temp targets. Evidence is activation flags and representative Temporary Target events. Uncertainty is how often high TT was used. Dependency: do not loosen activation while evening TBR is high. No component is null, so verify is not used.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: 3-minute UAM delivery and boost-sized SMBs are a leading explanation of the 16:00-19:00 overshoot, but this family is dependent with DynISF and is second to the overnight target. Evidence is interval 3 min, UAM 20 min, and sample SMB equals 0.4-1.6. Uncertainty is boost frequency. Dependency: do not change delivery in the same step as the target.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: These caps are loose versus about 19.7 U/day insulin and did not bind observed IOB near 5-6 U, so tightening them would not treat the current overnight lows and is not the first family. Evidence is max_iob 25, max_basal 12, enacted temps near 4 U/h. Uncertainty is how SMB caps reference max versus profile basal. Dependency: limits are brakes, not a substitute for the target change. No null component.

Autosens off is consistent. DynISF 70 percent is the operational ISF and likely contributes to high-BG stacking, but it is not separable from UAM delivery or profile ISF in this step. Evidence is DynISF on, variable_sens 28-124, Autosens false. A sensitivity_ratio of 1 is only a neutral snapshot. Dependency: hold DynISF while changing overnight target. No null component.

Carb-absorption settings were idle with zero carbs and COB 0. UAM deviation is not carb-impact evidence. Evidence is empty carb entries and unused COB. Uncertainty is complete for these numbers. Dependency: do not retune absorption to model unannounced meals.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Keep the observed unannounced-meal path: no supported prebolus, no supported immediate bolus percentage, continue SMB/UAM as the meal engine, and do not add e-carbs. Do not start a large pre-meal bolus on top of always-on UAM while 19:00 and overnight lows are active and DIA is 10 h.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Declared meal_strategies is empty and strategy_stable_for_period is null, which is an absent declaration rather than a Nightscout confirmation gap. Telemetry shows zero carbs, zero e-carbs, COB 0, and correction-sized doses around unannounced rises. That observed execution conflicts with any assumed wizard meal plan, so confidence in timing or percent splits stays low.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: For 3-5 usual afternoon eating events, record start time, whether any insulin was given before the first bite, and approximate carb grams.

exceptions.pattern: Recurring late-morning to afternoon rise after tiny correction-sized doses.
exceptions.suggestion: If those meals are later announced, test a modest pre-meal bolus rather than a CR change or more frequent SMB.
exceptions.rationale: Several windows rise for 2 hours after 0.05-0.35 U, showing late UAM rather than a tested CR.

exceptions.pattern: Same-day afternoon peak then evening crash, especially near GLP-1 notes, high UAM IOB, or 135 mg/dL temp targets.
exceptions.suggestion: Prefer a high temp target that keeps high-TT SMB off, not e-carbs and not a larger immediate bolus percent.
exceptions.rationale: Local 16:00 TAR then 19:00 TBR 15.3 percent fits stacked DynISF/UAM and long DIA more than missing e-carbs.

implementation_steps: Treat this as decision-support review only. Independently verify the active AAPS profile against the listed inventory before any edit.
Change one item only: profile target 00:00 from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL. Leave 23:00 target, all basal rates, CR, ISF, and DIA unchanged.
Do not change SMB interval, UAM caps, DynISF factor, Autosens, max IOB, or max basal in the same step.
Watch local 00:00-03:00 lows and 04:00-08:00 averages for several nights, and keep usual hypo treatment available.
If overnight time below range improves and 04:00-08:00 stays acceptable, only then consider a later single review of either 23:00 target or UAM/DynISF for the 16:00-19:00 crash, not both.

In parallel, log a few afternoon meal start times and rough carb amounts so prebolus, immediate percent, and e-carbs can be reviewed later. Do not introduce e-carbs or a large meal bolus while the target test is running.
education: UAM can dose unannounced meals when COB is 0; that is not the same as counting carbs twice.
With Dynamic ISF on, the loop often uses a much stronger or weaker ISF than the profile value of 56 mg/dL/U.
A 10-hour DIA means afternoon SMB can still be active at dinner and overnight, so a late low is not automatically a basal error.
Raising a target reduces how hard the loop drives toward 90 mg/dL; it is a different lever from cutting basal.
GLP-1 notes in the period can increase insulin effect even when profile numbers stay the same.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
Do not issue or apply automatic AAPS changes from this review. Discuss proposed settings with the care team.
Time below range is already 5.1 percent with lows to 41-42 mg/dL; do not add overnight or late-evening insulin to chase afternoon highs.
An occlusion and pump error were logged on 08-19; infusion-set and sensor issues can mimic profile failure.
The profile name indicates u200 dilute insulin, so displayed units may not match U100 assumptions; treat unit scaling as uncertain.
Do not disable UAM without a replacement meal-announcement plan.
